scenarios: two sessions of one tenant in one workspace under one configuration share a single server process: same pool key, same pid, sharers 2, one handshake in the server's own log
one changed byte of configuration is a different fingerprint and a different process
a different workspace root is a different pool entry and a different process
a different tenant is a different pool entry (key isolation)
a dead transport is never handed out again
proof: the sharing is observed as one operating-system process id reported to two sessions, with exactly one MCP handshake in the server's own record.
limitations: no idle eviction (servers live until the Core stops); health is handshake-and-still-open with no periodic ping; tenant isolation proven at the key because one Core serves one tenant, while the workspace field of the same key is proven end-to-end.
